transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… the main thing is my concentration’s gotten pretty unreliable. At the clinic I’ll be reviewing a chart, or even at home laying out a watercolor wash, and I suddenly realize I’ve read the same line three times. My mind just wanders off to everything that could go wrong.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

Yes… quite often. It’s not always one thing. My mind sort of keeps going around—old patients, whether they’re being looked after, the handoff of the practice, money, and… what I’m supposed to be useful for once I’m fully retired. It feels bigger than it should, honestly.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
I don’t know that I’d call it depressed. Maybe a bit flat some days, but… mostly it’s just worry, I think.
Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I get worked up, but not like a sudden surge that peaks like that within minutes.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?
I’m not really sure. I still do some things, but… I don’t know if I enjoy them the same way. I haven’t paid much attention to that.
Do you feel like you're still able to take pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I still do things here and there, but whether I’m taking much pleasure in them… I haven’t really thought about it that way.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but now you don't enjoy them at all?
I don’t know that I’d say “not at all.” I… haven’t really noticed it that clearly. I still do some of the same things, just maybe I don’t think much about whether I’m enjoying them.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly lost interest. I just haven’t really paid much attention to it, I guess.
Do you feel like you've been looking forward to things less often than you used to?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really kept track of that. I guess I just go day to day and don’t think much about whether I’m looking forward to things.
Do you feel like you've been taking less pleasure in activities that normally would be enjoyable for you?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed a big change that way. I still do things… I just don’t spend a lot of time thinking about whether I’m getting pleasure from them.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight lately?
Not that I’ve really noticed. My weight seems… about the same, as far as I can tell.
Do you feel like there are things that you used to find pleasurable, but now they don't bring you as much happiness as they used to?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that. Things feel about the same, I guess.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that came on very quickly?
Not really, no. I can’t think of a time where it came on suddenly like that.
Do you find that you've been worrying about things more days than not over the past six months?

Yes… more days than not, I’d say. My mind keeps going around things—old patients, whether the practice handoff is solid financially, what I’m going to be worth once I’m fully retired. It feels like more worry than the situation really calls for, honestly.
Is your worry present more days than not, and has it been that way for more than six months?
Yes. It’s been more days than not… probably since I started the formal retirement process, about a year and three months ago.
Do you feel like you're able to control your worry most of the time?

Not most of the time, no. I try to talk myself through it, like I would with a nervous patient, but then one concern turns into another. Before I know it I’m checking emails or going back over notes… or asking the same questions again instead of just letting it be.
Do you think your worry is disproportionate to the actual problems you're facing?
Yes… I think so. I mean, there are real things to sort out, but my mind keeps circling them—patients, the handoff, money, what I’ll be worth after retiring—and it feels bigger than it should be.
Is your worry usually about social situations or is it more about everyday things and various problems?

It’s more everyday things, I’d say. Not so much social situations. My mind just keeps circling around the practice, the patients, the money side of the handoff… and whether I’ll be of any use once I’m fully retired. It feels bigger than it should.
Has your worry been causing you significant distress or interfering with your daily life?

Yes… it has. I’ve had to slow down parts of the retirement handoff, even put some of it off, because I keep second-guessing myself and losing time at the clinic. And things I used to do to unwind, like painting or gardening, feel… less manageable than they used to.
